meta.label: Updated November 23, 2026
meta.label_basis: the build's own time (generated_at) as a calendar date in US Eastern time, the date a reader sees on the card

rules.week_now: the highest of the last graded week in weekly_actuals plus one, the latest week in weekly_transactions and the latest injury report week (at most 18), so one late grading run does not blank the newer files
rules.window: a transaction, new starter or role item is kept when its week is week_now or week_now minus 1; an injury item is kept from the team's latest report week when that week is week_now minus 2 or later, so a team just off a bye keeps its last report; a report week before week_now is written in the past tense
rules.teams: team codes are normalised before any join (LA to LAR and the older codes OAK, SD, STL, WSH, JAC); a code still unknown is listed in meta.unknown_teams and its rows are not used
rules.kinds: the kind order inside each group comes from data/team_changes_weights.json (card_kind_rank, counted from our own issues by scripts/count-team-change-kinds.js, plan part 6 step 4); with no usable weights file it is the plan's part 4 order, out_or_back first and role and roster_move level. No betting or draft kind exists
rules.order: plan part 4 as ruled by CoS 2026-11-19 15:31. First, a trade, signing or release of a player who matters (for a trade, one who matters to either team) always makes the card, newest first if more than five. Then, for the slots left, players who matter before players who do not, whatever the kind; within each group, kind rank, then the newer week, then the detail order below, then name
rules.matters: a depth chart starter now, a starter the state saw this season (including one who left the starting slots, so an injured starter still counts), a player the depth chart names in a slot's starter_reason ("promoted after: NAME (IR)"), matched to a gsis_id through that slot's candidates, or one of the team's top three in the graded column (fantasy_points_graded) in any of the last three graded weeks. Plan part 4 says graded usage; the graded points are the one usage measure the actuals file carries for every position (it stores no attempts or carries)
rules.detail_order: reserve, out, doubtful, back, activated, questionable, added, now_with, signed, released, new_starter, role_up, role_down
rules.cap: at most 5 items per team and one item per player per team (the first in the order)
rules.out_or_back: listed out, doubtful or questionable on the team's latest injury report week; back when listed out on the team's previous report week (a bye week is skipped) and, on the latest week, not listed out or doubtful while the availability file says active for the same team
rules.reserve: a STATUS_CHANGE from ACT or INA to RES in weekly_transactions; the list is named from the availability file (IR injured reserve, PUP physically unable to perform), otherwise "a reserve list"
rules.activated: a STATUS_CHANGE from RES to ACT (returned to the active roster), or from RES to INA while availability still places him on that team (came off a reserve list)
rules.signed: SIGNED with status ACT, a row that names no other team. Never used for a team change
rules.team_change: CoS ruling 2026-11-19: a TRADED_OR_CLAIMED row (the team changed between two weekly snapshots) with old_status ACT, INA, RES, CUT or DEV and new_status ACT, INA or RES is written as a team change on both cards: "Added <position> <name>, last with the <old team>, before week N." and "<Position> <name> is now with the <new team>, as of week N." Never signed, traded or claimed, because the snapshot cannot tell those apart (QA gate 2: Jacoby Brissett read CUT at ARI and was traded)
rules.released: RELEASED with last_status ACT, RES or INA, or a STATUS_CHANGE from one of those to CUT. Left out when the player is still on that team (availability, the depth chart or a weekly_actuals row for that team in that week or later), and every release in a team-week with more than 20 RELEASED rows is left out as a snapshot gap and listed in meta.skipped_release_weeks. Practice squad only moves are left out
rules.new_starter: a player in the team's depth chart starter slots who was not in them at the last build (state in data/team_changes_starters.json); the first build only records the starters; a starter who leaves the slots is kept in the state for the rest of the season, and when he returns his old record comes back with no new starter item
rules.role: wide receivers, tight ends and running backs with targets in the last graded week, against their average over up to three earlier games for the same team (at least two); up when 4 or more targets above the average and at least 6 targets; down when 4 or more below an average of at least 6. Targets only: the actuals file carries no carries
rules.sentences: fixed templates in our own words, positions written out in words; no source text is copied
